source.title: From Weights to Features: SAE-Guided Activation Regularization for LLM Continual Learning
source.authors: Evan Ning; Wei Xue; Dong Lou; Yi-Ke Guo

page_placements.theme: SAE feature directions as steering and causal handles (mixed)

record.tranche_reason: The study uses pretrained SAE dictionaries as a feature coordinate system for continual-learning regularization, but does not test feature splitting as dictionary size increases.
record.gate_note: The study does not compare SAE dictionary sizes, match features across dictionaries, or test whether child features partition a smaller feature's inputs. Continual-learning performance and mask-variant results are about the proposed method, not the claimed splitting behavior, so they are not recorded as rows. The auxiliary analyses of task-unit separability and collateral exposure are recorded as related findings, not tests of a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses fixed Gemma Scope 16k-width SAEs as a coordinate system for continual-learning regularization. It never varies dictionary size, matches features across SAEs, or examines parent/child firing or hierarchy. Its mechanistic analyses (task separability, collateral exposure) concern the method, not feature splitting.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE feature-space regularization beats weight-space regularizers on TRACE and MedCL, and that polysemanticity is a structural barrier to weight-space protection. They draw no conclusion about feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses fixed pretrained Gemma Scope 16k-width SAEs for continual-learning regularization; it does not train or compare SAEs of increasing dictionary size.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported separability and collateral-exposure values differ between TRACE and MedCL; per-layer and task-pair separability also varies, with the text reporting mean AUC rising from 0.67 at layer 9 to 0.75 at layer 31.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-5% task-relevant SAE decoder directions are linearly separable by task (AUC 0.87–0.88). Fisher-important MLP neuron directions are at chance (0.50).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Gemma-2 9B, task-relevant SAE features are more task-separable than task-relevant MLP neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Protecting the top-5% Fisher neurons gives collateral/intended exposure of 0.91–0.96. Protecting the top-5% SAE features gives 0.43–0.61.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-space protection is less concept-selective than SAE feature-space protection.

record.problems: The feature-structure analyses are limited to Gemma-2 9B; the paper says validation on Mistral-7B and Gemma-2 9B base is in progress. The continual-learning experiments use a single training seed. No analysis directly tests feature splitting.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for continual-learning benchmark scores, regularizer hyperparameter sweeps, mask-importance variants, per-layer figure AUCs, or storage projections: these do not test feature splitting or another listed version.

untested.parts: No SAE width sweep, no cross-size feature matching, no input-coverage or direction test.
Uses an open SAE release (Gemma Scope) on a 9B model but never tests splitting in it.
No test of nested families or concept hierarchy. The k-NN decoder propagation assumes, without testing, that decoder neighbours share concepts.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller ones.
No comparison of SAE objectives or Matryoshka SAEs.

record.verdict_notes: The neuron-to-SAE decomposition (median neuron draws on 500–1350 features) concerns polysemanticity, not splitting. The study is single-model (Gemma-2 9B-it), uses a single seed, and is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE size sweep, feature correspondence across sizes, input-partition test, or direction comparison.
No test of splitting across large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families, geometric closeness among split features, or a concept hierarchy.
No parent-child firing or absorption test, nor a comparison of size or sparsity as a remedy.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents.
No test of splitting as an artifact of the SAE objective or comparison with Matryoshka or other SAE objectives.

relation.reason: Applies SAE features for continual-learning regularization and does not test feature splitting.

tranche.reason: Uses fixed 16k-width Gemma Scope SAEs as a tool for regularization. It never varies dictionary size or tests splitting, hierarchy or absorption.

source_check.notes: Results are on Gemma-2 9B-it only, with 16k SAEs at layers 9/20/31. The Table 3/4 values pool task pairs (and layers for Table 4). The paper never mentions feature splitting, so T6/cites_only could also be defended, but either way there are no verdicts.

statements.correction: Text gives SAE-feature AUC 0.882 (TRACE) and 0.866 (MedCL); neuron AUC 0.498 (TRACE) and 0.502 (MedCL). Collateral ratios: weight protection 0.96 (MedCL), 0.91 (TRACE); feature protection 0.61 (MedCL), 0.43 (TRACE). Model is Gemma-2 9B-it.
